hmac-generator.formula:
HMAC(K, m) = H((K' xor opad) || H((K' xor ipad) || m))

K' = key padded to the hash block size
ipad = 0x36 repeated, opad = 0x5c repeated

keyFacts: HMAC is a keyed hash: it proves both integrity and authenticity of a message.
The construction nests two hash passes with padded key material (ipad/opad).

hmac-generator.quickAnswer: HMAC is a hash combined with a secret key: it proves a message was not modified and that the sender knows the key. APIs and webhooks use it to sign requests — the receiver recomputes the signature with the shared secret and compares. This tool computes HMAC-SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 in your browser.

hmac-generator.workedExample:
Message: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
Key: key
Algorithm: HMAC-SHA-256, hex output.

HMAC-SHA256("key", "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog")
= f7bc83f430538424b13298e6aa6fb143ef4d59a14946175997479dbc2d1a3cd8

This is the standard test vector — any correct HMAC implementation produces exactly this value. Change one character of the key or message and the signature changes completely.
